not_applies_when_en: The aspect ratio has to change; generation from scratch.

title_en: Pass a canvas of the target dimensions
content_en:
If a specific aspect ratio is needed for a new image and prompting does not produce it, the best practice is to provide a reference image with the correct dimensions as part of the prompt:
1. Image part: a blank (white) canvas of the target dimensions, passed before the text (for example 16:9 1280x720, 9:16 720x1280, 1:1 1024x1024).
2. Text: an explicit instruction tied to the canvas, for example "Render this scene on the provided canvas to match its 16:9 aspect ratio." or "make sure to use canvas for aspect ratio".
applies_when_en: A specific aspect ratio is needed for a new image, but the prompt text does not produce it (or the aspect ratio parameter is not available).
not_applies_when_en: The model or platform accepts the aspect_ratio parameter; it is more direct.
needs_from_prompt_en: the target aspect ratio or dimensions
caveats_en: Providing a blank canvas with specific dimensions guides the model to generate an image that fits that shape; this is an influence, not a guarantee. (models: nb25)
Canvas helper presets: 1:1 1024x1024, 3:4 768x1024, 4:3 1024x768, 9:16 720x1280, 16:9 1280x720 (notebook choice, not guaranteed output sizes). (models: nb25)
In the notebook the canvas is always referenced in the text too; no aspect-ratio config parameter is used. (models: nb25)
The prompting article controls aspect ratio only through prompt wording, the input image, the last uploaded image, or a correctly sized reference, never an API parameter. (models: nb25)
This is a recipe from the preview era, before the GA aspect_ratio parameter. (models: nb25)

examples.текст: A cinematic, wide-angle shot of a lone astronaut standing on a desolate alien planet, looking up at a swirling, colorful nebula. The planet's surface is rocky and red, and two moons are visible in the sky. Render this scene on the provided canvas to match its 16:9 aspect ratio.
examples.что_показывает_en: Scene prompt ending with an explicit instruction to render on the provided canvas to match its aspect ratio.

examples.текст: make sure to use canvas for aspect ratio
examples.что_показывает_en: Closing instruction sent as its own text part, tying the output to the canvas.

canaries_en: I need a 16:9 image but the model keeps giving me squares
Make it vertical 9:16, the prompt alone does not work

terms.значение_en: An empty image of the needed dimensions, passed before the text to set the shape of the result (2.5 recipe).

terms.термин: reference image with the correct dimensions
terms.значение_en: An image of the target size passed with the prompt to get a specific ratio.

title_en: End the template with the format sentence
content_en:
Closing sentence of a prompt template when the frame format is known:
The image should be in a [aspect ratio] format.

not_applies_when_en: The format is set only by a call parameter (disputed, see the prompt-text-versus-parameter core).

Most of the six text-to-image templates end with an aspect-ratio slot; the filled examples end with orientation words ("Vertical portrait orientation.", "Square image.", "Landscape."). (models: nb25)
The product FAQ builds prompts in layers and writes the ratio as text at the end, for example "... with 2:3 aspect ratio." (models: nb2)

title_en: Write the aspect ratio inside the prompt
content_en: The aspect ratio can be written inside the prompt text, usually at the end, in forms such as "16:9 aspect ratio", "Format 16:9", "in 16:9 format" or "landscape 16:9". The ratio can also be set by a call parameter in addition to the text.
applies_when_en: The prompt must state the frame format in words (especially for series and compositions from several references).
not_applies_when_en: The format is set only by a parameter (see the disputed prompt-text-versus-parameter core).
caveats_en: Wordings used in examples (verbatim): "16:9 aspect ratio"; "Format 16:9"; "Make the aspect ratio 16:9."; "The 16:9 poster is displayed on ..."; "in 16:9 format"; "generate one at a time, 16:9 each"; "Each frame should be a landscape 16:9"; "Each image should be a separate output in 16:9 format."; "16:9, make 10 versions, one at a time"; "AR: 16:9"; "with 2:3 aspect ratio"; a bare "16:9" at the end; "generate each image in a 1:1 aspect ratio"; "square aspect ratio"; "in an ultra-wide panoramic shot". (models: pro, nb2, lite, unspecified)
For series, the format is stated per frame together with count and order ("10 frames, one by one", "Generate 6 images one at a time"). (models: pro)
In a UI-based asset studio, aspect ratio is a prompt element and an edit prompt ("change aspect ratio"), with no API parameter; not to be transferred to the API without checking. (models: pro)
Next to the example prompts on the model showcase pages, the product blogs and the marketing guide, no separate aspect-ratio parameter is shown. (models: pro, nb2)

Counter-examples: a cookbook follow-up turn "in an ultra-wide panoramic shot" runs with aspect_ratio 16:9 in the config, and the page with the interleaved example also shows REST imageConfig.aspectRatio "16:9". (models: unspecified)
For Lite the only support is an interleaved example page that lists Lite among its models. (models: lite)

title_en: Change ratio by adjusting background, subject locked
content_en: To change the aspect ratio of an existing image, the edit prompt can state the target ratio, how to get there (reducing background, expanding background, or expanding the image downwards and upwards), and that the main subject "remains exactly locked in its current position".
applies_when_en: A finished image has to be converted to another aspect ratio (for another platform) without moving the main subject.
not_applies_when_en: Generation from scratch (the format is set right away); an edit that keeps the format.
caveats_en: Ratios requested in prompt text across the examples: 1:1, 4:3, 5:3, 1.85:1, 2.39:1, 2.75:1, 4:1, 9:16, 1:4; whether these are API-supported presets is not stated. (models: pro)
"Reducing background" is used for narrower targets, "expanding background" or "expanding image downwards and upwards" for wider or vertical ones (reading of the example sets). (models: pro)
In a UI-based asset studio, an input image with the prompt "change aspect ratio" generates three versions in different sizes (UI, not API). (models: pro)
